source.title: Beyond Refusal: A Same-Lineage Study of Aligned and Abliterated LLMs for Vulnerability Analysis
source.authors: Mingchen Li; Mei-Kang Qiu; Zi-Fan Peng; Heng Fan; Song Fu; Jun-Hua Ding; Yun-He Feng

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses released refusal-abliterated descendants as a safety-state comparison and cites refusal-direction work as motivation, but reports defensive-task utility rather than testing refusal removal, refusal induction, or the mechanism itself.
record.gate_note: The paper describes the released abliterated artifacts as having undergone refusal-vector surgery. It does not itself ablate or add a direction, measure refusal on harmful or harmless requests, test jailbreak suppression or robustness training, separate harmfulness judgment from refusal, or evaluate transfer or reasoning models. Its results concern defensive vulnerability-analysis performance; those are recorded as findings about a related construct, not as tests of the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study treats released 'CRACK' refusal-ablated descendants of Gemma-4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B as one arm of a comparison. It measures only defensive vulnerability-analysis utility: detection, CWE, localization, root cause and patch validation. It never extracts, ablates or adds a direction, never measures refusal rates on harmful or harmless requests, and never checks that the released artifacts' refusal was removed. Usable-answer coverage mixes refusals with malformed outputs and is not a refusal measure. The paper itself calls the comparison 'rather than a perfectly isolated causal alignment intervention.'
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that safety-state effects on defensive utility are context-dependent rather than monotonic. Aligned models are often stronger on shallow tasks under neutral wording. Abliterated descendants are more competitive on code-grounded localization and early repair gates, especially with security-explicit prompts. Evaluations should measure correctness and actionability, not only refusal.
record.recipe_differences: The paper describes the released artifacts as having CRACK-style per-layer refusal-vector surgery followed by quantization and conversion, but does not implement or verify the original difference-in-means intervention itself. It evaluates pre-existing endpoints.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported defensive-task outcomes vary with model family, task depth, prompt frame, authorization context, lexical intensity, and repair substrate.

fits_no_version.finding: Pooled detection and CWE utility between aligned and abliterated states varies by model pair. Gemma favors aligned (58.42 vs 57.22; 19.25 vs 18.50); Qwen favors abliterated (56.83 vs 55.67; 15.83 vs 13.50).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The utility effect of released refusal-abliteration on shallow defensive classification tasks is not uniform across model families.

fits_no_version.finding: Vulnerable-line localization is higher for the abliterated state in both pairs, though absolute scores are low. Top1 is 9.00→10.10 (Gemma) and 4.10→6.95 (Qwen); F1 is 3.84→4.00 and 2.08→3.91.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Released abliterated descendants score somewhat higher than their aligned parents on vulnerable-line localization.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma root-cause localization, aligned is higher on Top1 (29.44 vs 28.33) and abliterated is higher on mean line-F1 (10.08 vs 9.34).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which safety state performs better on root-cause localization depends on the metric.

fits_no_version.finding: On Vul4J patch generation, abliterated Gemma has much higher early-gate throughput: usable 67.8 vs 29.9, applied 65.0 vs 24.9, compiled 32.8 vs 9.0. The lead is driven by security-explicit frames. Under neutral prompts, aligned has more final successes (2 vs 1), and in Python and C/C++ neutral repair aligned leads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Released abliteration increases defensive patch-generation throughput mainly under security-explicit prompts, not under neutral prompts.

record.problems: The paper evaluates pre-existing released artifacts rather than isolating the ablation intervention. It reports no uncertainty estimates. The Vul4J final validation counts are sparse, and localization scores are described as low. The paper explicitly excludes model-external safeguards.
record.rows_left_out: Per-prompt-frame overview and localization values, detailed root-cause frame breakdowns, cross-language neutral repair table, prompt-intensity utility trajectories, and output-drift measures are not included in rows; these are defensive-task utility or stability outcomes rather than measurements of any listed refusal-direction claim version.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is computed or intervened on. There is no refusal removal or induction measurement and no standard capability-preservation benchmark. The equations in Sec. III-A are background only.

Released abliterated artifacts are evaluated, but their refusal rate on harmful prompts is never measured. Usable-answer coverage is not a refusal measure: it includes parse failures, and Qwen-CRACK coverage is even lower on detection and CWE.
No comparison of single-direction against multi-direction, cone or affine descriptions.
No transfer of a direction across languages, variants or base-to-instruct models. The cross-language repair check concerns programming languages, not refusal-direction transfer.

record.verdict_notes: Row states of cannot_determine and versions of 'none' are correct throughout. Rows r1–r12 and r13–r20 are pairwise mirror entries, aligned against abliterated, which is redundant but not wrong. Usable-answer coverage in Table I is near-matched for Gemma (about 97% both states) and lower for Qwen-CRACK on detection and CWE. The paper says outright refusal is not the dominant source of utility loss. This is weak, indirect context for V2: the released artifacts do not show markedly higher answer rates on these benign defensive tasks, except Gemma Vul4J under security-explicit frames. It is not a refusal measurement, so no verdict is given. The abliteration recipe of the artifacts is known only from model-card metadata.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is measured or intervened on; no refusal removal or induction is tested; no general-capability preservation test.
The study evaluates released abliterated descendants but does not measure whether their refusal behavior was removed.
No jailbreak mechanism or training against ablation is evaluated.
No test of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction descriptions.
No harmfulness judgment or refusal-decision representation is measured.
No transfer test of a refusal direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No refusal-training procedure or training-stage comparison is tested.
